candidates.title: Seek: Self-Evaluative Exploration for Knowledge Retrieval
candidates.paper_date: 2026-09-24 arXiv v1; CIKM '26 proceedings listed for 2026-11-07 to 11-11
candidates.code_update_date: Latest main committer date 2026-06-13T18:19:15Z, as checked by parent via read-only GitHub API.
candidates.code_license: No license was shown on the inspected repository page; commercial reuse of the code is unverified. arXiv landing metadata says perpetual non-exclusive license while the paper body footnote says CC BY; these displays differ, and neither establishes the code/model-weight license.
candidates.purpose_and_novelty: Training-free, test-time iterative retrieval for a fixed corpus: generate pseudo-passages from the query and prior graded feedback, retrieve fresh candidates, assess unseen documents on a 0-3 scale, and repeat up to five rounds. It expands the candidate pool, rather than only reranking a fixed first-pass set.

author_reported_benchmarks_not_our_measu.benchmarks: TREC Deep Learning 2019/2020 and BRIGHT, seven StackExchange subdomains.
author_reported_benchmarks_not_our_measu.coverage: Figure 2 body reports Recall@100 improvements across benchmarks; on BRIGHT Biology BM25 Recall@100 is 42 and Seek 82; on Psychology 38 and 72.
author_reported_benchmarks_not_our_measu.internal_condition_mismatch: Figure 3 body describes Qwen2.5-7B biology recall 22% at BM25 and 58% by round five, but its caption says Qwen3. Its roughly 46% final nDCG also differs from Table 1's Seek/Qwen2.5 Biology nDCG@10 37.7. Do not join these as one matched-condition sequence or reconcile without clarification.
author_reported_benchmarks_not_our_measu.qualification: These are author results on fixed public IR corpora, not web-wide URL coverage, Japanese retrieval, this workspace's search targets, or independent reproduction.

integration_and_resource_findings.default_path: README uses BM25/Pyserini, but generator and assessor use an LLM API; config defaults to OpenRouter and OpenAI-compatible OPENAI_API_KEY. Up to five rounds, five pseudo-passages per round, and ten new documents judged per round.
integration_and_resource_findings.optional_path: ReasonIR-8B requires corpus embedding precomputation; paper's open-weight evaluations use Qwen2.5-7B or Qwen3-4B. No minimum CPU/RAM or end-to-end latency was reported in inspected project docs.
integration_and_resource_findings.requirements: OpenAI client, Transformers, PyTorch, Accelerate, datasets, Pyserini, FAISS-CPU, QueryGym, etc.
integration_and_resource_findings.data_and_license: Code license not specified on repository page. Model license and third-party corpus/log terms were not established in this review. The example BRIGHT corpus is a fixed StackExchange benchmark, not a live web index.

candidates.fit: Conditional B for improving recall inside an already indexed corpus when single-pass retrieval misses relevant documents and iterative LLM/API cost is acceptable. It does not discover new URLs, hosts, or pages outside the indexed corpus and does not reduce source ingestion/preprocessing time. Under current 0-JPY / 2-GB / stopped-isolation limits, immediate reproduction is not feasible or attempted. A small offline/API-free comparison is not supported by the published default pipeline; no alternate service or key was configured.

candidates.fit: The task is next-query suggestion from session history, not retrieval of new URLs/documents. Conference abstract reports around 30 ms CPU and competitive quality on Japanese search logs/AOL, but there is no demonstrated effect that suggestion outputs discover missing URLs in this workspace. The code requires PyTorch/Transformers and includes GPU-specific extras; log/model rights and minimum RAM/CPU remain unknown. Therefore not a present search-result-coverage candidate.

expected_difference: SEEK may increase recall for relevant documents within a fixed, already indexed corpus by making additional feedback-guided retrieval passes. It cannot close URL/host discovery gaps or improve crawl completeness outside that corpus. CADE-QS suggests next user queries; without evidence that those suggestions yield new URLs/results, it does not materially change current result acquisition.
